notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware or upstream simulator was attached or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's swimmer.xml, the model the card's entry symbol mjrl.envs.swimmer:SwimmerEnv constructs (swimmer.py:8), as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. The entry symbol was confirmed in the clone at mjrl/envs/swimmer.py:6 and registered at mjrl/envs/__init__.py:13-17. The MJCF has two torso slide joints and one torso hinge plus the hinge chain j1 to j4 (swimmer.xml:29-52), so the bridge state has 7 qpos and 7 qvel values, and four motor actuators (swimmer.xml:59-63), so cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [4 numbers]}}. The four motors state no ctrlrange of their own; the global default class gives motors ctrllimited=true ctrlrange=-1 1 (swimmer.xml:6-8), so the bridge derives the four -1 to 1 control bounds from the model (upstream_code, ref mjrl/envs/assets/swimmer.xml:actuator_ctrlrange), the same actuator_ctrlrange array the upstream builds its action Box from (mujoco_env.py:56-59). No bound is invented and no operator-required limit exists, so there is no site-limits.example.json. <option timestep="0.005"> (swimmer.xml:16) gives a 5 ms lockstep step; cap.world.reset.v1 calls mj_resetData + mj_forward and restores the model defaults. There is no hardware backend for a simulator, and the package declares no @reset and no re-enable (the bridge reset changes only the simulation).

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card's family-config decision and MujocoDriver helper express the MJCF model, so there is no deviation from the card. The legacy gym and mujoco-py task layer above the model is not expressible by the MuJoCo bridge: its step returns reward -10 times the change of qpos[0] and done False (swimmer.py:11-22), its observation is qpos[2:] plus qvel (swimmer.py:24-28), its reset draws qpos[2] from -pi to pi (swimmer.py:30-35), and gym registration adds max_episode_steps 500 (__init__.py:13-17). Those are NOT COVERED and are listed in the fidelity gaps; the primary control and stepping interface (data.ctrl + mj_step, reset) is preserved at model level. The package reads the model from the read-only clone in place and never imports or installs it; the clone was not modified.

FAKE: MuJoCo and mujoco-py are not installed and cannot be installed here (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library (fake.py, lock backends .fake:FakeMujoco). It parses the same MJCF for the joint layout, actuator count, inherited control ranges and option time step, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint; it loads no mesh, resolves no contact, water, camera or sensor, ignores the motor gear, and provides no mj_getState/mj_setState, so the bridge uses its basic checkpoint profile. The fake's F0 contract is published through fidelity_by_backend (engine analytic:stand-in mujoco module (no physics)); the class-level fidelity describes the real engine (F1). A backend name not listed (sim) would import the real mujoco module and load the same file; that path was not run. The fake returns the real model sizes (7 qpos, 7 qvel, 4 ctrl); nothing is truncated.

GATE WARNINGS (all expected and not failures): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is a module stand-in object, so the gate has no recorded native surface to compare (the bridge-boundary behaviour checks still ran); G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived integer inputs ticks and seed and the numeric action.ctrl elements, whose bounds are the model's control range in the model's own units. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. No hardware was attached, no --backend hardware or --allow-hardware was used, and no human review or hardware test is claimed.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Checked all facts, the selected swimmer MJCF and inherited control ranges, lock/provenance, licence, fake surface and software stop/reset behavior against the pin. fake.py now integrates the four gear-20 motors as efforts against placeholder unit inertia instead of tracking ctrl as joint positions; test_driver.py adds a regression that failed on the original and passes after the fix. Updated driver.py and facts.md to disclose the corrected F0 effort semantics and omitted body/fluid/constraint dynamics, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The final fake gate passes G1-G9 with contract_checked evidence, and collect.py --strict exits 0; RESULT.json, task.json and driver.lock.json were left unchanged. For the human reviewer: Only swimmer.xml is served; the card's peg_insertion.xml, point_mass.xml and sawyer.xml models are excluded. This is model-level control, not the legacy SwimmerEnv task/reward/random-reset/time-limit interface. The F0 fake uses independent unit inertias and omits fluid drag, coupling and joint-limit forces; no MuJoCo trajectory or hardware was run. The software stop fences lockstep stepping and retains ctrl/state; releasing the latch performs no step, and a later explicit step can reuse the stored controls. The swimmer model header requires keeping its LICENSE with it; no upstream model or assets were copied.
